objective_pt: Use common idiomatic phrasal verbs naturally in conversation (come up with, put up with, run into, figure out, end up), including separable word order ("figure it out", not "figure out it").

teacher.goal_pt: Show how phrasal verbs make speech sound natural compared with Latin-based verbs.
prompts: Which sounds more natural in a chat: "I encountered an old friend" or "I ran into an old friend"?
What's something you can't put up with?
watchFor: Avoiding phrasal verbs completely and choosing Latin-based words (tolerate, discover, invent).
Pronoun after the particle: "pick up it".

exercises.prompt: I ran into an old friend and we ended up talking for hours.
accepted: I ran into an old friend and we ended up talking for hours

exercises.instruction_pt: Which sentence has the correct word order?
exercises.explanation_pt: With separable phrasal verbs, a pronoun must go between the verb and the particle: "pick it up".

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English, with a phrasal verb: "Eu não aguento mais esse barulho."
accepted: I can't put up with this noise anymore
I can't put up with this noise any more
I can't put up with this noise any longer
I can't stand this noise anymore
I can't take this noise anymore
I can't bear this noise anymore
I can't deal with this noise anymore

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Suportar" (tolerate) is "put up with", "stand" or "bear". "Support" means "apoiar" (false friend).
commonErrors.correction_en: I can't put up with this noise anymore.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Put up with" is a three-part phrasal verb; don't drop "with".
commonErrors.correction_en: I can't put up with this noise anymore.

teacher.goal_pt: High-frequency phrasal verbs: come up with, figure out, end up, run into, bring up, turn down, look into.
prompts: What did you end up doing last weekend?
Have you ever turned down a job offer?

exercises.example_en: She came up with a brilliant solution.
We ended up staying until midnight.
He turned down the offer because of the salary.

exercises.instruction_pt: Match each phrasal verb with its meaning.
Say this in natural English, with a phrasal verb: "A gente acabou ficando em casa."
accepted: We ended up staying at home
We ended up staying home
We ended up staying in
In the end, we stayed at home
We ended up just staying at home
We wound up staying home

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "End up" is followed by the "-ing" form: "ended up staying".
commonErrors.correction_en: We ended up staying at home.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Acabar fazendo" is "end up doing". "Finish" means to complete something.
commonErrors.correction_en: We ended up staying at home.

teacher.goal_pt: Stress in phrasal verbs: the particle is usually stressed (come UP with, turn DOWN, figure it OUT).
prompts: Say "I'll figure it out" with stress on "out".
watchFor: Stressing the verb and swallowing the particle, which hides the meaning.
Pausing between the verb and the particle instead of linking them.

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat. Stress the particle: figure it OUT.
exercises.prompt: Don't worry, we'll figure it out.
accepted: Don't worry, we'll figure it out
Don't worry, we will figure it out

commonErrors.explanation_pt: A pronoun goes between the verb and the particle: "figure it out".
commonErrors.correction_en: Don't worry, we'll figure it out.

exercises.prompt: They offered me the job, but I turned it down.
accepted: They offered me the job, but I turned it down

exercises.instruction_pt: In "She brought it up at the meeting", which word gets the most stress?
exercises.explanation_pt: In phrasal verbs, the particle usually carries the stress: brought it UP.

teacher.goal_pt: Understand phrasal verbs in fast, connected speech and answer using them.
prompts: Which phrasal verbs did you hear?
Can you answer with a phrasal verb too?
watchFor: Missing the particle in fast speech, which changes the meaning completely.
Answering with a Latin-based verb that sounds stiff.

exercises.listen: We were halfway there when we ran out of petrol, so we ended up hitching a lift with a farmer.
options: They ran to the petrol station.
They had no petrol left and got a ride from a farmer.
They decided to stay at a farm.
exercises.explanation_pt: "Run out of" = have none left; "hitch a lift" = get a free ride from someone.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen and answer using "come up with".
exercises.listen: Has anyone thought of a name for the new product yet?
accepted: Not yet, but we're trying to come up with one
No, we haven't come up with one yet
We haven't come up with anything yet
Not yet. We're still trying to come up with something
Yes, Ana came up with a great one
Yes, the team came up with a few ideas
No one has come up with a name yet
Nobody has come up with one yet

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Don't drop "with": "come up with one".
commonErrors.correction_en: Not yet, but we're trying to come up with one.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: No double negatives: "Nobody has come up with one", not "Nobody hasn't".
commonErrors.correction_en: Nobody has come up with one yet.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen and say you'll investigate, using "look into".
exercises.listen: The client says the invoice is wrong. Can you check?
accepted: Sure, I'll look into it
I'll look into it
Of course, I'll look into it right away
No problem, I'll look into it
I'll look into it and get back to you
Sure, let me look into it
Leave it with me, I'll look into it

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Look into" is inseparable: the object goes after it: "look into it".
commonErrors.correction_en: Sure, I'll look into it.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Look for" = procurar; "look at" = olhar. To investigate a problem is "look into".
commonErrors.correction_en: Sure, I'll look into it.

teacher.goal_pt: Hold a natural chat about recent events that pushes the learner to use phrasal verbs.
prompts: Have you had to put up with anything annoying lately?
What's a problem you've figured out recently?
Who did you last run into by chance?

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English, with a phrasal verb: "Ela puxou esse assunto na reunião."
accepted: She brought that up in the meeting
She brought it up in the meeting
She brought up that subject in the meeting
She brought up that topic at the meeting
She brought that up at the meeting
She brought it up at the meeting
She raised that in the meeting

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Puxar um assunto" is "bring something up" or "raise", not "pull".
commonErrors.correction_en: She brought that up in the meeting.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: With a pronoun, put it in the middle: "brought it up" / "brought that up".
commonErrors.correction_en: She brought that up in the meeting.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English, with a phrasal verb: "Ficamos sem tempo, então vamos adiar."
accepted: We've run out of time, so let's put it off
We ran out of time, so let's put it off
We've run out of time, so let's postpone it
We've run out of time, so we'll put it off
We've run out of time, so let's push it back
We're out of time, so let's put it off
We've run out of time, so let's leave it for later

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Ficar sem" is "run out of": "we've run out of time".
commonErrors.correction_en: We've run out of time, so let's put it off.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Pronoun in the middle: "put it off".
commonErrors.correction_en: We've run out of time, so let's put it off.

accepted: I'm looking forward to catching up with you

exercises.instruction_pt: Answer in about a minute, using at least four phrasal verbs from the unit.
exercises.prompt_en: Tell me about a plan that didn't work out the way you expected. What happened, and what did you end up doing?
guidelines_pt: Use "end up" + -ing for the unexpected result.
Include at least three of: come up with, run into, figure out, turn down, put off, run out of.
Put pronouns in the middle: "figure it out", "put it off".
Close with what you learned: "Looking back...".

teacher.goal_pt: Quick-fire phrasal verb recall and word order check.
prompts: Tell me about a plan that fell through, using two phrasal verbs.

exercises.instruction_pt: Replace the formal verb with a phrasal verb and say it: "I rejected their invitation."
accepted: I turned down their invitation
I turned their invitation down
I turned it down
I turned down the invitation

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Turn off" is for switching off a device. To reject an offer is "turn down".
commonErrors.correction_en: I turned down their invitation.

accepted: of

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Run out of" + noun.
commonErrors.correction_en: We've run out of milk again.

exercises.explanation_pt: "Look into" is inseparable: the object always comes after the particle.

exercises.prompt: It all worked out in the end.
accepted: It all worked out in the end
It all worked out fine in the end

practice.example_en: I finally got round to fixing the bike.
They backed out of the deal at the last moment.
I spent Sunday catching up on my reading.
My sister talked me into going to the party.

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat with natural rhythm and stress.
practice.prompt: I keep meaning to call her, but I never get round to it.
accepted: I keep meaning to call her, but I never get round to it
I keep meaning to call her, but I never get around to it

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat with natural rhythm and stress.
practice.prompt: He backed out at the last minute.
accepted: He backed out at the last minute
He backed out at the very last minute

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat with natural rhythm and stress.
practice.prompt: I need a weekend to catch up on sleep.
accepted: I need a weekend to catch up on sleep
I need a weekend to catch up on some sleep

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat with natural rhythm and stress.
practice.prompt: She talked me into signing up for a marathon.
accepted: She talked me into signing up for a marathon
She talked me into signing up for the marathon

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat with natural rhythm and stress.
practice.prompt: Let's not rule anything out just yet.
accepted: Let's not rule anything out just yet
Let's not rule anything out yet

practice.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English, with a phrasal verb: "Eu dei de cara com meu ex no mercado."
accepted: I bumped into my ex at the supermarket
I ran into my ex at the supermarket
I bumped into my ex at the market
I ran into my ex at the market
I bumped into my ex in the supermarket
I ran into my ex in the supermarket
I came across my ex at the supermarket
I ran into my ex at the grocery store
I bumped into my ex at the grocery store

commonErrors.explanation_pt: For meeting someone by chance, use "bump into" or "run into".
commonErrors.correction_en: I bumped into my ex at the supermarket.

practice.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English, with a phrasal verb: "Preciso pôr em dia meus e-mails."
accepted: I need to catch up on my emails
I have to catch up on my emails
I've got to catch up on my emails
I need to catch up with my emails
I need to get through my emails
I need to get on top of my emails

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Pôr em dia" is "catch up on", not a literal "put in day".
commonErrors.correction_en: I need to catch up on my emails.

practice.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English, with a phrasal verb: "Ela desistiu do curso no meio."
accepted: She dropped out of the course halfway through
She dropped out of the course in the middle
She dropped out halfway through the course
She gave up the course halfway through
She quit the course halfway through
She gave up on the course halfway through
She dropped out of the course midway through

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Desistir" is "give up" or "drop out". "Desist" is formal and means to stop doing something.
commonErrors.correction_en: She dropped out of the course halfway through.

practice.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English, with a phrasal verb: "Vamos ter que cancelar a festa."
accepted: We'll have to call off the party
We'll have to call the party off
We're going to have to call off the party
We're going to have to call the party off
We'll have to cancel the party
We will have to call off the party
We're gonna have to call off the party

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Call out" means to criticise publicly. To cancel is "call off".
commonErrors.correction_en: We'll have to call off the party.

practice.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English, with a phrasal verb: "Eu não consigo entender o que ele quer."
accepted: I can't figure out what he wants
I can't work out what he wants
I can't make out what he wants
I just can't figure out what he wants
I can't figure out what he's after
I can't work out what he's after
I cannot figure out what he wants
I can't understand what he wants

commonErrors.explanation_pt: In an indirect question, use statement order: "what he wants".
commonErrors.correction_en: I can't figure out what he wants.

practice.instruction_pt: Listen and answer with a phrasal verb: you decided not to accept it.
practice.listen: What happened with the job offer in Lisbon?
accepted: I turned it down
I ended up turning it down
I decided to turn it down
In the end, I turned it down
I turned the offer down
I turned down the offer
I ended up turning down the offer
Actually, I turned it down

commonErrors.explanation_pt: With a pronoun, it goes in the middle: "turned it down".
commonErrors.correction_en: I turned it down.

practice.instruction_pt: Listen and explain with a phrasal verb: your car broke down on the motorway.
accepted: My car broke down on the motorway
My car broke down on the highway
The car broke down on the motorway
Sorry, my car broke down on the motorway
Sorry, my car broke down on the highway
My car broke down on the way here
My car broke down on the freeway

commonErrors.explanation_pt: A car "breaks down". Without "down", "break" means to smash.
commonErrors.correction_en: My car broke down on the motorway.

practice.instruction_pt: Listen and answer with a phrasal verb: you've come up with a couple of ideas.
practice.listen: Have you thought about how to fund the project?
accepted: Yes, I've come up with a couple of ideas
I've come up with a couple of ideas
Yes, I've come up with a few ideas
Yes, I came up with a couple of ideas
I've come up with a couple of options
Yes, I've come up with a couple of possibilities
I have come up with a couple of ideas

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Ter uma ideia" is "come up with" an idea. Don't drop "up".
commonErrors.correction_en: I've come up with a couple of ideas.

practice.instruction_pt: Talk for about a minute, using at least five phrasal verbs.
practice.prompt_en: Tell me about a plan that didn't work out the way you expected.
guidelines_pt: Use phrasal verbs for the plan: "We set out to...", "We'd been looking forward to...".
Explain what went wrong: "...fell through", "...broke down", "...ran out of...".
Say how it ended: "We ended up...".
Reflect: "In the end, it all worked out."

practice.instruction_pt: Role-play: make plans with a friend, using phrasal verbs naturally.
practice.scene_pt: You and a friend planned a camping trip, but the weather forecast is bad.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: So, are we still going camping this weekend?

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Say you're not sure, because it might rain, so you might have to put it off.
accepted: I'm not sure. The forecast says it might rain, so we might have to put it off
I'm not sure, because the forecast says it might rain, so we might have to put it off
Not sure. It might rain, so we might have to put it off
I'm not sure. It might rain, so we may have to put it off
I'm not sure. The forecast says it might rain, so we might have to put it back
I'm not sure. It looks like rain, so we might have to put it off

commonErrors.explanation_pt: With a pronoun, it goes in the middle: "put it off".
commonErrors.correction_en: We might have to put it off.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: Oh no. Tom's really looking forward to it.

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Say you know, and you don't want to let him down.
accepted: I know, and I don't want to let him down
I know. I don't want to let him down
I know, I really don't want to let him down
I know, and I'd hate to let him down
I know, and I don't want to disappoint him
I know, we don't want to let him down

commonErrors.explanation_pt: With a pronoun, it goes in the middle: "let him down".
commonErrors.correction_en: I don't want to let him down.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: Maybe we could find somewhere indoors instead?

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Say good idea, you'll look into it tonight.
accepted: Good idea. I'll look into it tonight
That's a good idea. I'll look into it tonight
Great idea. I'll look into it this evening
Good idea. I'll look into some options tonight
Good thinking. I'll look into it tonight

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Investigar / verificar" is "look into". "Look after" means "cuidar de".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'll look into it tonight.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: Perfect. Let me know what you come up with.

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Say you will, and you'll get back to her tomorrow.
accepted: I will. I'll get back to you tomorrow
Will do. I'll get back to you tomorrow
Sure, I'll get back to you tomorrow
I will, and I'll get back to you tomorrow
Of course. I'll get back to you tomorrow
Sure thing. I'll get back to you tomorrow

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Te dar um retorno" is "get back to you".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'll get back to you tomorrow.

practice.instruction_pt: Which sentence is correct?
options: I'll pick up you at eight.
I'll pick you up at eight.
I'll you pick up at eight.
practice.explanation_pt: With a pronoun object, separable phrasal verbs put it in the middle: "pick you up".

practice.instruction_pt: What does "to get round to something" mean?
options: To finally find time to do it
practice.explanation_pt: If you get round to something, you finally do it after delaying it.

practice.instruction_pt: Listen. What did they do in the end?
practice.listen: We were supposed to go to the beach, but we ended up staying in and watching films.
practice.explanation_pt: "We ended up staying in" means they stayed at home, even though it wasn't the plan.

practice.instruction_pt: Complete with one word.
practice.sentence: We've run ___ of milk. Can you get some?
accepted: out

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Ficar sem" is "run out of".
commonErrors.correction_en: We've run out of milk.

practice.instruction_pt: Complete with one word.
practice.sentence: How do you put ___ with his constant complaining?
accepted: up

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Aguentar, tolerar" is "put up with".
commonErrors.correction_en: How do you put up with it?

practice.instruction_pt: Put the words in order to make a sentence with two phrasal verbs.
accepted: I'll look into it and get back to you

practice.instruction_pt: Match each phrasal verb with its meaning.
